lines: +run-name: "Generative UI Engine ${{ inputs.is_release && 'publish' || 'build' }} ${{ inputs.version }} from ${{ github.ref_name }} by @${{ github.actor }}"
+# Publishes `opik-genui` to npm and to PyPI from one build of one commit, so the
+# two packages of a version always carry the same contract and guidance.
+# Manual only for now: it is not part of the Opik release, so it cannot block one.
+# Run it after an Opik release, with that release's version, to publish the engine
+# at the same version. Without `is_release` it builds, checks and proves the PyPI
+# Trusted publishing (OIDC), no stored tokens. Both registries have THIS file,
+# `genui_publish.yml`, registered as the trusted publisher for `opik-genui`, for
+#   npm  validates the *entry-point* workflow, the one that started the run.
+#   PyPI validates the workflow that contains the job (`job_workflow_ref`).
+# Renaming this file breaks both until the registrations are changed. When this
+# becomes a job of the release, npm needs `release-wrapper-release-n-deploy.yml`
+# registered as well; PyPI needs nothing new.
+        description: Opik release version to publish the engine as (X.Y.Z). A release builds the tag of that version.
+        description: Publish to npm and PyPI. When off, build and check the branch this run is started from and upload nothing.
+  # Retry transient PyPI/network failures longer before failing the build.
+      # Mints the OIDC token both registries exchange for a short-lived publish
+      # Read via env, never `${{ }}` substitution inside a script.
+            echo "::error title=Validate inputs::version='${RELEASE_VERSION}' is not X.Y.Z. PyPI and npm must receive the same version string."
+            echo "::error title=Validate inputs::a release must be started from main (got ${REF}). Run without is_release to try a branch."
+        # A release builds the tag, so the packages hold exactly what that Opik
+        # release holds. Any other run builds the branch it was started from.
+          # npm trusted publishing (OIDC) needs npm >= 11.5.1, which Node 26 bundles.
+          # No caches in a job that publishes: a poisoned cache would ship.
+        # js/package.json is the one version source: the build writes it into the
+        # Python package data and the wheel build refuses data of another version.
+        # Mints a PyPI upload token from this workflow's OIDC identity and discards
+        # it. Runs before anything is uploaded, so a wrong PyPI registration cannot
+        # leave npm published and PyPI not. Same check as build_and_publish_sdk.yaml.
+        # npm has no equivalent: its publisher is first exercised by the publish.
+          # Tokens go via stdin, never argv; a 200 body holds a live upload
+          # token, so it lands in a 0600 mktemp file removed on exit.
+            # Error bodies carry no token, only codes like invalid-publisher.
+            echo "::error title=PyPI preflight::Trusted Publishing rejected this workflow (HTTP ${CODE}): $(jq -c '.errors // .' "$MINT")"
+          echo "OK: PyPI accepts this workflow as a Trusted Publisher for opik-genui."
+        # setup-node writes an empty `_authToken` stub that npm would try before
+          # A rerun after npm published and PyPI failed must not fail here, or the
+          # PyPI step below could never be retried.
+            echo "::notice title=Publish to npm::opik-genui@${RELEASE_VERSION} is already on npm; skipping."
+            # `if pipeline` keeps a failed attempt from ending the step; see
+            if timeout 180 npm publish -w opik-genui --access public 2>&1 | tee "$PUBLISH_LOG"; then
+              echo "::notice title=Publish to npm::opik-genui@${RELEASE_VERSION} is already on npm; skipping."
+          echo "::error title=Publish to npm::npm publish failed after 3 attempts."
+          # Off on purpose: PyPI rejects the attestation once this runs as a called
+          # workflow of the release (pypi/warehouse#11096), and the two ways of
+          # running it should publish the same thing.
+            echo "**Not a release:** built and checked, nothing uploaded. PyPI accepted this workflow as a trusted publisher."
- `styles.css`: the host-side stylesheet for the frame, the loading and the error state, every rule under `.ov-view`.

- `js/libraries/`: one entry per library a view may declare, built into `dist/libraries/<name>.js` as one script that sets its globals. The host fetches the file and the contract inlines it after the bootstrap, only for a view that declares it.

-- `python/`: the `opik-genui` Python package: `ENGINE_VERSION`, `AREAS`, `MAX_HTML_LENGTH`, `TOKENS` and `prompt(area)`, read from `python/src/opik_genui/data/` (git-ignored, written by `npm run build`).

+- `js/scripts/`: `emit.ts` writes `python/src/opik_genui/data/` (`engine.json`, `prompt-<area>.txt`); `licenses.ts` writes `dist/libraries/<name>.licenses.txt`, the licences of every package a library bundle contains; `smoke.ts` is the test suite.

+- `python/`: the `opik-genui` Python package: `__version__`, `ENGINE_VERSION`, `AREAS`, `MAX_HTML_LENGTH`, `TOKENS` and `prompt(area)`, read from `python/src/opik_genui/data/` (git-ignored, written by `npm run build`).
- `dev-host/`: a page that renders a fixture view through `ViewHost`, and `dev-host/check.mjs`, the browser check.
- Not a new contract: a new token, a new token value, a change to the guidance, a host-side change in `HtmlFrame.tsx`, `ViewHost.tsx` or `styles.css` that keeps the messages the same.
- A new contract ships with Opik first; Ollie and opik-mcp move to it by upgrading their pin of the packages.

+- Both packages are published by hand with `.github/workflows/genui_publish.yml` ("Run workflow" on `main` with `is_release`), not by the Opik release, so a failed publish cannot block one. Give it the version of an Opik release that already happened: it builds that release's tag once and publishes `opik-genui` to npm and then to PyPI with that version.

+- Without `is_release` (off by default, as in the SDK publish workflows) it builds and checks the branch it is started from, proves the PyPI registration and uploads nothing. Run it that way before the first release and after any change to the workflow or the packaging.

+- `js/package.json` is the only version source. The workflow sets it at build time, the build writes it into `engine.json`, the Python package reads it from there, and the wheel build fails on data built for another version. The version in the repository stays `0.1.0` and is never published.

+- Auth is trusted publishing (OIDC). `genui_publish.yml` is the registered publisher on both registries: npm matches the workflow that starts the run, PyPI the workflow that contains the job. Renaming the file breaks both until the registrations are changed. Moving the publish into the Opik release needs a second npm publisher, `release-wrapper-release-n-deploy.yml`.
+- A version cannot be published twice. A rerun skips a package that is already on its registry.
+- What ships: `js/package.json` `files` and `exports` for npm, `python/pyproject.toml` for PyPI. A new entry point or library needs an `exports` entry; a library bundle ships with its licences file.
- An area is where a view is shown, such as `widget`, a dashboard grid cell. It is fixed when the view is created, and each area gets its own authoring prompt from `prompt(area)`.
| Python `opik-genui` (`python/`) | the guidance and versions that `npm run build` emits into `python/src/opik_genui/data/` | Ollie backend, opik-mcp |
-Neither package is published yet. The Opik frontend will build against `js/` in this repository; Ollie and opik-mcp will pin released versions once the packages ship with the Opik release jobs.

+Both packages are published together by one manual workflow, with the version of an Opik release, so a version of one always matches the same version of the other. The Opik frontend builds against `js/` in this repository; Ollie and opik-mcp pin released versions.

+The engine behind [Opik](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik) views. A view is HTML, CSS and script written by a model; it carries no data and declares inputs that the host resolves. This package renders a view in a sandboxed iframe, the same way in every host.
+React 19 is a peer dependency. The version of this package is the Opik release it shipped with.
+Keep `fetchInput` and `fetchLibrary` stable: a new function identity means fetch again.
+| `opik-genui/ViewHost` | The host component. It refuses a view it cannot render, resolves the inputs, loads the declared libraries and mounts the frame. |
+| `opik-genui/HtmlFrame` | The iframe host on its own, for a caller that already has the data. |
+| `opik-genui/contract` | The HTML contract per `engine_version` and `ENGINE_VERSION`, the latest one. |
+| `opik-genui/tokens` | The `--ov-` token values for light and dark. |
+| `opik-genui/view` | The view and input types, the areas, the libraries and the size caps. |

+| `opik-genui/libraries/vega.js` | Vega, Vega-Lite and Vega-Embed as one script, for a view that declares the `vega` library. Serve the file from your own origin and return its text from `fetchLibrary`. |
+- Limit `frame-src` (or `child-src`) in the page's Content Security Policy to your own origins. A view that navigates itself is stopped by the host page, not by the view's sandbox.
+- A library bundle contains third-party code. Its licences are in `opik-genui/libraries/<name>.licenses.txt`; ship that file with the bundle.
+Apache-2.0. Authoring guidance for the model that writes the views is in the Python package of the same name.
+  "description": "Opik generative UI engine: the sandboxed iframe host and HTML contract for model-written views",
